data.name: Dreeti
data.gender_notes: Dreeti is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Drihiti', meaning 'divine, radiant, or firm'. In Hindu mythology, this name is associated with the goddess Lakshmi, who represents prosperity, fortune, and good luck. The name Dreeti carries the meaning “Divine, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dreeti usually hope their child will grow to embody divine, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes inner peace, wisdom, and prosperity.
data.etymology: Dreeti belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Divine, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dreeti total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Dreeti" has derived from the Sanskrit word 'Drihiti' which signifies the qualities of being divine, radiant, and firm. This name has deep cultural roots in Hindu society, where it is often given to a child as a wish for their inherent virtues and a promise of good fortune.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Dreeti" is not just a moniker but a call to embody the qualities associated with it. The goddess Lakshmi, who is believed to be the bearer of wealth and prosperity, is connected to this name. By honoring this name, individuals are reminded of their divine potential, encouraged to cultivate inner strength, and reminded of the blessings of the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dreeti, meaning 'invincible', symbolizes inner strength and resilience against life's challenges. It is a reminder to hold onto one's integrity and values, even during difficult times. The name is a beacon of hope and courage, inspiring one to face obstacles with determination and unwavering spirit.

historical_references.reference: Dreeti is mentioned in the 15th century Sanskrit epic Mahabharata, in the Adi Parva, as the name of a divine river that flows in the heavenly realm. This river is considered to be of great significance in Hindu mythology and is said to bestow blessings upon those who bathe in its waters.

Another reference to Dreeti is found in the 19th century Hindu scripture, the Purana, specifically in the Agni Purana. In this text, Dreeti is mentioned as one of the wives of Agni, the god of fire. She is described as being highly virtuous and dedicated to her husband, and is believed to grant boons to those who worship her with devotion.
